blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Aloft Hotels commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Select-service lifestyle: modern rooms, social lobby energy, and tech-forward cues for urban and airport-adjacent travelers inside Marriott Bonvoy. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus Moxy's budget lifestyle intensity and AC Hotels' European contemporary select-service, Aloft sits in modern lifestyle select-service without W-level luxury capital.

blocks.title: Channels
blocks.body: Brand.com / Marriott Bonvoy app · major OTAs · GDS · metasearch (where active for the hotel)

blocks.title: Campaigns
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy and parent portfolio campaigns where the hotel is eligible

blocks.title: B2B Programs
blocks.body: Corporate, SME, and RFP programs routed through parent sales infrastructure where active for this flag

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Model Aloft Hotels contribution after loyalty chargebacks, preferred-agency commissions, and local competitive set reality—not headline RevPAR alone.

blocks.title: Distribution & Channel Mix
blocks.body: Parent central reservations, Marriott Bonvoy app, and designated online channels—confirm commission structures and rate parity obligations in the current agreement exhibit.

blocks.title: Revenue Management
blocks.body: Parent revenue tools and Marriott Bonvoy demand signals support pricing experiments; owners still need property-level strategy for this brand's product promise.

blocks.title: Digital Marketing & Performance Media
blocks.body: Paid and owned media templates at portfolio scale, with creative that must still feel brand- and hotel-specific rather than generic parent advertising.

blocks.title: Corporate, SME & Group Pull
blocks.body: Contracted travelers, small meetings, and negotiated programs where Aloft Hotels fits the account's brand ladder.

blocks.title: Owner Perception Risk
blocks.body: Owners sometimes expect lifestyle lightness without systems cost; Aloft Hotels still carries parent systems, Marriott Bonvoy economics, and brand QA. Align IC expectations early.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: Aloft Hotels participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy at Aloft Hotels

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Aloft Hotels. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including Aloft Hotels, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy partnerships, co-branded cards, and bonus campaigns expand the loyalty halo; Aloft Hotels stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy drives distribution and repeat demand but adds loyalty chargebacks and program economics. Underwrite net contribution after loyalty—not membership vanity metrics.

blocks.title: P&L Implications
blocks.body: Loyalty assessments and program contribution affect net rooms revenue. Use current agreement exhibits; do not invent undisclosed rates.

blocks.title: Operating Implications
blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support Marriott Bonvoy enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications
blocks.body: Parent property and reservation systems integration is required for Marriott Bonvoy participation—budget cutover and training in the conversion plan.

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of repeat Aloft stays where the hotel already competes on product fit—not on a standardized prototype alone.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help Aloft hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping brand positioning intact.

blocks.title: Elite Member Value
blocks.body: Elite recognition (upgrades where available, late checkout, milestone rewards) supports contribution at Aloft; amenity delivery still varies by property capability.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: Bonvoy recognition across Marriott sister brands matters for guests who split stays within the network—Aloft remains the brand-specific node inside that earn/redeem graph.

blocks.title: Cobrand & Payment Scale
blocks.body: Bonvoy co-branded cards, Moments, and bonus-point campaigns lift acquisition; model hotel-level contribution after loyalty chargebacks—not portfolio vanity metrics.

blocks.title: Corporate & Small Meetings
blocks.body: Marriott account linkage and negotiated transient patterns support midweek compression where corporate and SMERF mix fits the Aloft asset—confirm for this hotel's source markets.

blocks.title: To Join
blocks.body: Aloft application, royalty, program contribution, and Bonvoy assessments — confirm current Marriott franchise / development fee exhibits. Amounts are not staged without a verified disclosure.

blocks.title: To Operate
blocks.body: Steady-state royalty, program contribution, and Marriott Bonvoy loyalty assessments — confirm definitions, bases, and current percentages in the live disclosure exhibit for Aloft Hotels. Do not underwrite from peer rumor.

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.title: Fee Variability
blocks.body: Initial vs conversion paths differ; program contribution and loyalty assessments may change by year under agreement terms. Lock the fee exhibit before IC—never extrapolate from a peer hotel's rumor. Geography note: Confirm current Marriott franchise / development disclosure for Aloft

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain Aloft Hotels's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Select-service lifestyle: modern rooms, social lobby energy, and tech-forward cues for urban and airport-adjacent travelers inside Marriott Bonvoy.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.

blocks.title: Urban & Airport Lifestyle Select-Service
blocks.body: Urban and airport-adjacent assets where social lobby energy and modern rooms can lift select-service demand with Bonvoy distribution.

blocks.title: Mixed-Use Lifestyle Anchors
blocks.body: Mixed-use sites seeking lifestyle select-service without full-service capital—underwrite public-space programming carefully.

blocks.title: Sibling Clarity Versus Moxy & AC
blocks.body: Assets that need diligence against Moxy and AC Hotels before assuming the same owner use case or fee path.

blocks.title: Gateway Urban
blocks.body: Strong Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Aloft Hotels fits gateway urban demand where parent distribution and loyalty support transient and corporate mixes—underwrite city competitive set.

blocks.title: Conversion & Repositioning
blocks.body: Strong Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Conversion / repositioning is a core owner path when independents seek Aloft Hotels affiliation and loyalty access—underwrite PIP scope first.

blocks.title: Corporate-Led Urban
blocks.body: Moderate Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Corporate-led urban accounts can pull Aloft Hotels when the product matches account brand ladders; confirm negotiated rates before assuming contracted volume.

blocks.title: Regional & Secondary Markets
blocks.body: Moderate Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Secondary markets work when Aloft Hotels's product and fee load clear local ADR reality; diligence source-market seasonality.

blocks.title: Highway & Interstate Transient
blocks.body: Not a Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Highway / interstate limited-service economics generally sit outside Aloft Hotels's product and fee structure.

blocks.title: Resort & Coastal Leisure
blocks.body: Limited Fit
blocks.demandScenarioDescription: Leisure resort fit depends on whether Aloft Hotels's service model matches resort operating complexity.
